extracted.intended_audience: applicants and attorneys filing European patent applications at the EPO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the formal and conformity requirements a European patent application must meet before grant, focusing on acknowledging prior art, claim form, reference signs, and aligning the description with claims under the EPC and EPO practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of background art (Rule 42(1)(b) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall 'indicate the background art which, as far as is known to the applicant, can be regarded as useful to understand the invention, draw up the European search report and examine the European patent application, and, preferably, cite the documents reflecting such art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention relevant prior art (especially earlier patent applications), preferably cite documents (e.g. a patent publication number) and provide a short summary of what that document discloses. This amendment is often requested by the EPO after search; it can be a brief statement. If the applicant did not know of the prior art at filing, the requirement still applies once the EPO identifies relevant documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend description to indicate most relevant prior art when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Once novel and inventive claims have been arrived at, the EPO will usually require the description to be amended to indicate at least the most relevant prior art (if not already present) to meet Rule 42(1)(b) EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO may issue an examination report or include the amendment in a communication of intention to grant. The amendment can be brief (citation + short summary). Applicants should comply or consider whether to contest; failure to amend may lead to further communication or examination steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must define technical features (Rule 43(1) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought in terms of the technical features of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, claims should contain a statement indicating the subject-matter designation and those technical features necessary for definition that form part of the prior art, and a characterising portion specifying the technical features for which protection is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present independent claims in the two-part form where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent claims very often appear in two-part form: a preamble describing features forming part of the prior art and a characterising part beginning with 'characterised in that' or 'characterised by' specifying the novel features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the two-part form when it clearly distinguishes known features from the characterising features. The EPC requires this 'wherever appropriate'—the EPO may itself amend claims into two-part form in an intention-to-grant communication. Accepting such amendments can be pragmatic to obtain grant, absent other substantive objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions when two-part form is inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-part form should not be used if it would give a distorted or misleading picture of the invention or prior art, for example if the invention lies solely in the combination of known elements of equal status; if it is a modification by omission or substitution; or if it is a complex system where the invention resides in changes in several parts or their inter-relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also avoid two-part form when the only relevant prior art is novelty-only prior art. If inappropriate, clearly acknowledge prior art in the description instead. Weigh risks of admitting preamble features are in prior art before voluntarily adopting two-part form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of admissions when adopting two-part form
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting claims in two-part form may be seen as an admission that the features in the preamble are indeed found in the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant disagrees or prefers not to admit that the preamble features are in the prior art, they may resist amendment; if the applicant amends claims themselves and a dispute later arises, it may be difficult to argue otherwise. Consider strategic implications before accepting or making two-part amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference signs in claims (Rule 43(7) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application contains drawings including reference signs, technical features in the claims shall preferably be followed by such reference signs (in parentheses) if intelligibility is thereby increased; these reference signs shall not be construed as limiting the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference signs' sole function is to increase intelligibility. It is generally sufficient to include the reference sign at the first instance of a feature in each claim rather than every occurrence. Applicants may note in the description that reference signs are non-limiting. EPO practice often treats inclusion of reference signs as mandatory and may insert them; the requirement can be lifted only if claims without them are shown to be clear under Article 84 EPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conform the description to the claims (support and consistency; Article 84 and Article 69(1) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent can only be granted where the claimed invention is supported by the description. Claims must be interpreted in light of the description, and inconsistencies between description and claims must be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If independent claims are amended to introduce limitations, the description must be amended to make clear those formerly-optional features are essential. Subject matter falling outside the scope of the claims (for example after amendments) must be indicated as not part of the claimed invention or deleted. Failure to amend as required can lead to summons to oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle excluded subject-matter in the description (Article 53 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any subject-matter excluded from patentability under Article 53 EPC must be removed, reworded so it no longer relates to excluded subject-matter, or prominently marked to make it clear it does not form part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to matter contrary to ordre public or morality, plant or animal varieties and essentially biological processes, and methods of treatment of the human or animal body. If protection is desired for such subject-matter present in the application as filed, consider filing a divisional directed to that subject-matter before the parent application is finally disposed of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications timing and strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant seeks protection for subject-matter not claimed in the (to-be-granted) application but disclosed in the application as filed, they should consider filing a divisional application directed to that subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional applications must be filed before the earlier patent application is finally granted, refused, abandoned, withdrawn, or deemed to be withdrawn. Use divisionals to preserve claim scope for different subject-matter rather than leaving it in the description only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical note: EPO communications may include amended text
rubrics_metrics.description: In some cases the EPO will include amended description or claims in a communication indicating an intention to grant (i.e., the Examining Division may itself amend text to comply with formal requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Examining Division has amended the text (e.g., to two-part form or to add reference signs), it may be pragmatic to accept the amended text to obtain grant unless there are other substantive amendments needed. Not all suggested amendments are absolutely required in every case; evaluate strategically.
